input.quote: 21.1 Except for Excluded Claims, each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the Fees paid or payable by Customer under the first Order Form during the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim.
input.rationale: The structure of Section 21 is acceptable: the cap is expressly mutual (21.1), the exclusion of indirect and consequential damages is mutual (21.2), and "Excluded Claims" (21.3) carves out confidentiality, data-protection and security, indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement. The failure is the cap base: "Fees" is defined at 1.5 as only the "Implementation Fee", fixed by 1.6 as a one-time USD 12,000 charge in the first Order Form, and 21.1 further narrows it to that first Order Form — so recurring subscription and services charges fall outside the base and the cap is an illusory USD 12,000, below the six-month floor and in walk-away territory. The redline resets limb (a) to the fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim, adds the USD 1,000,000 limb, and broadens the 21.3 payment carve-out from "undisputed Fees for conforming Services" to all amounts due under the Agreement, leaving mutuality, the damages exclusion and the carve-outs untouched.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] "Fees" is defined as only the one-time USD 12,000 Implementation Fee under the first Order Form, so the cap is illusory; we have reset limb (a) to the fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and added the USD 1,000,000 limb. We also broadened 21.3 so all amounts due from Customer, not just undisputed Fees for conforming Services, are outside the cap.
